title.value: Reincarnating Reinforcement Learning: Reusing Prior Computation to Accelerate Progress
title.justification: The title of the paper is clear and concise, explicitly stating the core topic of the research, which is the reuse of prior computation in reinforcement learning to accelerate progress.
title.quote: Reincarnating Reinforcement Learning: Reusing Prior Computation to Accelerate Progress

extractions.description: This paper introduces the concept of reincarnating reinforcement learning (RRL), focusing on reusing or transferring prior computational work to accelerate the development of RL systems. The authors propose a specific method called QDagger to efficiently transfer knowledge from a suboptimal policy to a value-based RL agent, demonstrating the method's effectiveness in various scenarios, including gaming and real-world applications such as balloon navigation.

climate_change_is_central.justification: Climate change is not addressed as a theme in the paper. The focus is on reinforcement learning techniques and their application to improving computational efficiency, not on environmental concerns.
climate_change_is_central.quote: The inefficiency of deep RL typically excludes researchers without access to industrial-scale resources from tackling computationally-demanding problems. To address these issues, we present reincarnating RL as an alternative workflow or class of problem settings, where prior computational work (e.g., learned policies) is reused or transferred between design iterations of an RL agent, or from one RL agent to another.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address climate change or related topics; its primary focus is on the efficiency of RL systems in different computational settings.
primary_category.quote: To address both the computational and sample inefficiencies of tabula rasa RL, we present reincarnating RL (RRL) as an alternative research workflow or class of problems to focus on.

secondary_categories.justification: As the primary category is not related to climate change, secondary categories are also not applicable in this context.
secondary_categories.quote: The focus is entirely on reinforcement learning methodologies and improvements.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific climate change sub-category as its focus is on computational methods and efficiency.
primary_sub_category.quote: The prevailing trend in RL research is to learn systems that can operate efficiently tabula rasa, that is without much learned knowledge including prior computational work such as offline datasets or learned policies.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Since no primary sub-category related to climate change is applicable, secondary sub-categories are also not relevant.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The study and classifications in the paper do not touch on climate change themes.

applications.justification: The application of RL to navigating stratospheric balloons is mentioned as a real-world problem addressed using the proposed method, showing practical usage beyond theoretical improvements.
applications.quote: Equipped with QDagger, we demonstrate the sample and compute-efficiency gains of reincarnating RL over tabula rasa RL, on ALE, a humanoid locomotion task and the simulated real-world problem of navigating stratospheric balloons [11] (Section 5).

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories effectively cover the scope of climate-related research, and this paper does not introduce a new primary category concerning climate change.
new_primary_category.quote: Reincarnating RL can democratize research by allowing the broader community to tackle larger-scale and complex RL problems without requiring excessive computational resources.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on reinforcement learning and computational techniques, not introducing new sub-categories in the context of climate change.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: RRL seeks to maximally leverage existing computational work, such as learned network weights and collected data, to accelerate training across design iterations of an RL agent or when moving from one agent to another.
